newsitem.title: FRANCE: Moslem guerrillas slaughter 18 villagers- paper.
newsitem.headline: Moslem guerrillas slaughter 18 villagers- paper.

text.p: An Algerian newspaper said on Tuesday Moslem guerrillas cut the throats of 18 people in a remote hamlet southwest of the capital Algiers.
Among the 18 peasants were a four-year-old child and a six-month-old baby, El Watan daily said.
The rebels attacked the defenceless village at Mouzaia area, 60 km (40 miles) southwest of Algiers, during the night last week and after killing the 18 inhabitants set their homes ablaze, it said.
"Following the victims' burial on Thursday, local people mobilised themselves to hunt down the murderers, to arm the local population and ensure protection of remote communities," El Watan said.

The massacre report came in a long overview of the security situation by El Watan's main specialist on the conflict who urged Algerians to keep vigilant and not be lured into complacency by a relative lull of violence in recent weeks.

The report said the rebels, suffering shortages of weapons and manpower, had lost the initiative over attacks against protected targets and were now only able to hit remote areas to make their presence known.
About 60,000 people have died in Algeria since early 1992 when violence erupted after the authorities cancelled a general election dominated by Islamic fundamentalists.
More than 90 villagers were slaughtered by Moslem guerrillas last month, a few hours before the start of a three-week-long campaign by candidates for June 5 general elections.

Radical Islamists were barred from the poll but moderate Moslem militants were allowed to compete and won 103 seat in the 380-member National Assembly in which the pro-President Liamine Zeroual National Democratic Rally (RND) took 156 seats.
